subject: arts-music
unit_title: Advanced Studio Practice and Personal Direction
lesson_title: Concept model A: advanced composition and visual hierarchy

rubric.exceeds: All five evidence groups are present: guided pair, original three-form study with named focal point, two named variables, preserved intermediate state plus path check and revision decision, and evidence-based reflection and critique.
rubric.meets: All required evidence is present; one note may be brief, but the guided pair, original study, two variables, intermediate state, path check, revision decision, reflection, and critique can each be located.
rubric.developing: The independent visual study is present, but one or two required evidence parts are missing or cannot be located, such as the intermediate state, path check, revision decision, reflection, or critique.
rubric.beginning: The submitted evidence does not yet include an independent three-form visual study with a named focal point, or several required process parts are absent.

rubric.exceeds: At least two hierarchy variables work together to establish the intended first stop and a readable later route; the learner precisely locates the strongest relationships and explains a meaningful tradeoff.
rubric.meets: At least two named variables create observable emphasis related to the intended focal point, and the learner cites where the eye or hand moves next using evidence from the work.
rubric.developing: Hierarchy variables are attempted, but the stated route and the observable relationships only partly align, or the explanation names variables without locating their effect in the work.
rubric.beginning: The work or explanation does not yet show a testable intended order of attention. This is a signal for focused reteaching, not a judgment about style or ability.

rubric.exceeds: The learner makes a coherent, evidence-supported case for the chosen hierarchy and recognizes another defensible reading or a deliberate ambiguity without treating it as failure.
rubric.meets: The learner states the intended order and connects specific value, scale, placement, isolation, repetition, edge, or direction evidence to that intention.
rubric.developing: The intended order is stated, but several claims rely on preference or general praise instead of observable evidence from specific locations.
rubric.beginning: The response does not yet state an intention or connect a reading to observable evidence; no particular style, subject, mood, or arrangement is required.

rubric.exceeds: The intermediate state, path check, and later state show what was tested; the learner isolates a variable, evaluates its effect, and gives an evidence-based reason to revise or deliberately keep the result.
rubric.meets: The record shows an intermediate state, one criteria-based check, and a learner-chosen revision or reasoned decision to keep the work.
rubric.developing: A change is documented, but the record does not yet make clear what evidence prompted it or which hierarchy variable changed.
rubric.beginning: No intermediate state or revision decision is visible yet. Invite a small fresh test; do not direct the learner’s aesthetic choice or complete the work.

scoring_judgment_guidance: Score the submitted evidence against the four focus-specific dimensions. First record objective presence without judging polish. For hierarchy, intent, and revision, cite a location or process fact from the learner’s work. Do not compare the work with the model’s shapes, arrangement, palette, mood, or style. If the observed path differs from the learner’s first intention, accept a reasoned revision of either the work or the stated intention. A reviewer may offer options, but the learner owns the final choice. Record NOT_YET_EVIDENCED when evidence is absent; never infer talent, care, motivation, diagnosis, or character.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task on advanced composition and visual hierarchy.
The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name a next step.
formative_check: Explain the modelled approach to advanced composition and visual hierarchy in your own words and name the step most likely to go wrong.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: There is no fixed composition or answer for advanced composition and visual hierarchy. Score the authored objective constraints and the focus-specific rubric evidence; accept materially different creative, performance, design, or interpretive choices when the learner supports them against the criteria.
mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use sketch or rehearsal record, created or performed work, artist statement, critique response, revision log, and portfolio reflection; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.

mastery_interpretation.secure: At least 85% with accurate independent application and adequate evidence and reasoning.
mastery_interpretation.developing: 70–84% or inconsistent explanation; assign targeted review and a fresh transfer check.
mastery_interpretation.not_yet: Below 70% or a missing prerequisite; reteach the smallest gap and reassess with new evidence.
mastery_interpretation.rule: A unit score is one evidence source, not the sole basis for long-term mastery.

unit_assessment_reference.note: This lesson is one session inside the unit; the unit assessment record above is the summative instrument, and this lesson rubric scores only this session's evidence.

remediation_plan: Route 1: Reduce the work to a three-value map. Label each major area light, middle, or dark; circle every large jump. Keep one large jump and lower the others in a fresh thumbnail. Use three forms and only pencil pressure. Create one dark-light jump at the intended first stop; keep the other forms middle or pale. Check yourself: Squint or use the tactile value labels: can you locate one strongest difference? New attempt: Make a new thumbnail with different placements and run a new three-second check. Route 2: Cover the work except for the intended focal point and one competing area. Compare only those two; choose whether value, scale, isolation, edge, or direction should separate them. On scrap paper, redraw the two areas and change exactly one chosen variable. Check yourself: Name the changed variable before deciding which area arrives first. New attempt: Return all areas in a fresh thumbnail and test the intended path without the model in view.
extension_plan: Apply advanced composition and visual hierarchy under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on advanced composition and visual hierarchy rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
accommodation_note: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task centres a visual element (advanced composition and visual hierarchy). Provide tactile, raised-line, or high-relief equivalents, enlarged and high-contrast print, and a verbal description route. Never make colour discrimination alone carry a criterion — pair any colour judgement with value, label, or texture.

Any model, source, or artifact under study is supplied in an accessible parallel form: text alternative or transcript, described version, and a tactile or enlarged rendering where the original is visual. The learner is never required to perceive the source in one specific channel to analyse it.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.

source_integrity.note: The complete required learner resource is attached in the task package as ma-resource:ma-g9-arts-and-music-u01-l02. It is Manuel Academy original, CC BY 4.0, contains no third-party content, and requires no external source, paid tool, specialized material, instrument, recording, or public presentation.

safety_and_privacy.note: No public performance, camera, voice recording, photograph, or audience is required at any point; a private option and a written/no-audio alternative are stated in the task package and score identically.

standards: Michigan Arts Education Standards: Visual Arts — Creating
objective_constraints: Use three or more forms or areas.
Name one intended focal point before developing the study.
Use at least two hierarchy variables.
Run one visual-path check and make or deliberately decline one revision with a reason.
legitimate_variation: Difference from the Academy model is never an error and resemblance earns no extra credit.
Subject, abstraction, medium, format, style, palette, and mood remain learner-owned choices.
A focal point may be created through value, scale, placement, isolation, repetition, edge, direction, or another defensible visual relationship.
A learner may support a steep, subtle, distributed, ambiguous, or deliberately nonhierarchical route when the evidence matches the stated intent.
A learner may revise the artwork, revise the stated intention, or keep the result with an evidence-based reason.
